why: The other half of the same defect, and independently sufficient to cause it: `setState`'s close-all putting `--hidden` on a surface that is mid-crossfade. These four calls were bare `classList.add`s that bypassed the transition contract entirely, so the Back handlers' `setState` slammed the pane `showX(false)` was fading. Reverting EITHER this or `panel-close-collapsed-by-its-own-setstate` above reproduces the cut on its own -- measured, both directions -- which is why both exist as separate entries rather than one. The skip is safe because closure is still guaranteed: a surface passed over here is hidden by its own settle, and gameplay entry (where 150ms later would be too late) goes through `setState`'s own `instant` transition, whose drain settles it in the same frame. `crossfades a panel CLOSE, not only its open` is the case that measures it, at the assertion that the closing pane keeps its `--hidden` OFF while it fades. Scoped to hud.test.ts; expectFailures counts that scoped run only.
killedBy: createHud application transition contract crossfades a panel CLOSE, not only its open
